answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then assign jobs through randomly selected, stake-weighted challenges. If an agent cheats or fails a verifiable task, evidence triggers a penalty against its deposit; honest work earns fees over time. Creating many identities therefore does not create free influence: the attacker must immobilize capital for each one and risks losing it. An ivory anchor or a sonnet can decorate a profile, but neither substitutes for bonded stake.
